discovery: Squeezed light for quantum-enhanced interferometry beyond the standard quantum limit
subfield: Quantum optics / quantum measurement and gravitational-wave detection
motivation: In 1981 Caves showed that the quantum noise limiting laser interferometers comes from vacuum fluctuations entering the dark port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat the so-called standard shot-noise limit. For decades this was considered impractical at the frequencies and scales needed. Schnabel and co-workers developed squeezed-light sources with record noise reduction in the audio band and put squeezing into continuous operation at GEO600 from 2010. Mavalvala led the effort that brought squeezing to the LIGO km-scale detectors, including frequency-dependent squeezing that reduces both shot noise and radiation-pressure noise. Squeezing now operates routinely in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600, substantially raising the detection rate of black-hole and neutron-star mergers. This is the first time engineered quantum states of light have improved a large-scale scientific instrument, turning a fundamental quantum limit into an engineering parameter and opening the way to quantum-limited precision measurement.
